name_reason: Complies with fd2_<domain>_<descriptor>. '35' is the per-event handler-table dispatch index 0x35 (xref site 0x51C65), a domain ID, not an address residue. Descriptor corrected from '__unref_dialog_with_state' to '__ch23_mech_boss_defeat': the slot is LIVE, reached via the ch23 kill-drop path -- ch23 char_spawn_record[2] = the mech boss (機甲隊長, enemy_data 48, char_id 0x74, lv22; runtime slot 0x12) carries pickup_kind=2 param=0x35, so its death dispatches consequence[0x35], showing the mech's shutdown line (page 5) then mass-killing runtime slots 0x12..end (the mech squad shuts down). The earlier 'unref' verdict only scanned turn-event/tile-step hooks and missed the kill-drop path.
purpose: Chapter 23 mech-boss-defeat / squad-shutdown (dispatch slot 0x35, reached via the ch23 kill-drop path when the mech boss record[2] enemy_data 48, pickup_kind=2 param=0x35, runtime slot 0x12, falls): show dialog page 5 (the mech's shutdown line), then mass-kill every runtime_char_array slot from index 0x12 to the end (the whole mech squad shuts down; cinematic terminator-style wipe).
logic_summary: After the Watcom __CHK stack probe (frame 0x28), calls fd2_display_dialog_scene(current_chapter_text, page=5, 0xA0000, 0x140, 0xCD, 0x4C, 0x4A, 0x13, 1) to render dialog page 5, then fd2_kill_runtime_chars_from_index_to_end(0x12) which sets wHP_current=0 for runtime_char_array[0x12..party_member_count-1] and plays the death animation once. The dispatch event_arg is never read. In the binary the kill call hosts a Class-3 shared tail at 0x35354 (CALL fd2_kill_runtime_chars_from_index_to_end; ADD ESP,4; RET) that fd2_chapter_event_handler_53 JMPs into to reuse the cleanup tail; that tail-merge is a binary size optimisation with no source-level effect.

params.semantics: Dispatch-table event argument. The per-event handler table @ 0x51B91 invokes each slot as 1-arg cdecl void fn(uint event_arg); this handler does not read it. The live Ghidra name 'stepping_char_id' is a __CHK stack-probe artifact and is misleading.
params.reason: Ghidra's 'stepping_char_id' is an artifact name produced by the __CHK stack probe and does not match the dispatch-table convention (the arg is the generic event_arg, not a stepping char id). The source declaration already uses 'event_arg', matching all sibling handlers. Rename applied in Stage 2.

notes: Source comment block (chevt2.c lines 295-314) is already precise and accurate; matches the disassembly (PUSH 1/0x13/0x4A/0x4C/0xCD/0x140/0xA0000/page=5/text; CALL display_dialog_scene; ADD ESP,0x24; PUSH 0x12; CALL kill_from_index; ADD ESP,4; RET) and the kill callee's documented behavior (hp_current=0 for slots idx..count-1 then one death animation).
